events.text: Stephenson's Rocket wins the Rainhill Trials for the Liverpool and Manchester Railway
The first production Ford Model T is built in Detroit
Karl von Drais shows his pedal-less Laufmaschine, forerunner of the bicycle, in Mannheim
Karl Benz applies to patent his Motorwagen and drives it publicly in Mannheim

reveal.explanation: Mannheim saw both the two-wheeled running machine of 1817 and, nearly seventy years later, Benz's first drive in a motor car. In between, Rocket showed that a locomotive could beat a stationary engine, and by 1908 Ford was building the car that would put much of the world on wheels.

sources.excerpt: It is regarded as the first bicycle and von Drais is seen as the "father of the bicycle", but it did not have pedals. Von Drais introduced it to the public in Mannheim in 1817 and in Paris in 1818.

Stephenson's Rocket is an early steam locomotive of 0-2-2 wheel arrangement. It was built for and won the Rainhill Trials of the Liverpool and Manchester Railway (L&MR), held in October 1829 to show that improved locomotives would be more efficient than stationary steam engines.

Benz continued to work on his Motorwagen and on 29 January 1886 he submitted the patent application for an "automobile fueled by gas". He first tested it on public roads in the early summer of 1886 and drove it publicly on the Ringstrasse in Mannheim on 3 July 1886.
The first production Model T was built on August 12, 1908, and left the factory on September 27, 1908, at the Ford Piquette Avenue Plant in Detroit, Michigan.
